correctness.rationale: Each graph is exactly KG(5,2), and all k-cut faces are independently enumerated by disconnected-complement witnesses and downward closure. The finite verifier checks every directed Hasse incidence and acyclicity of two discrete Morse matchings for each k=2,...,7. For k=5, complete signed integral 8x12 (reverse 10x14) Morse boundaries have seven (reverse nine) unit Smith factors; thus H3=Z, H4=Z^5. A 2-connected 3-skeleton and integral Hurewicz classification of attaching degrees upgrade to S3 wedge five S4. Other k have only one critical 0-cell and single dimension of spheres, or a zero degree graph differential; k>=8 void. The complete script and deterministic replay output are included.

originality.rationale: The original 2023 paper includes the Petersen 2-cut graph and broad classes not containing the new 5-cut. The 2024 sequel considers grid/squared path/disjoint unions, not this graph. Earlier finite results resolve k=3,4 and are not claimed as novel; the general girth-k+2 theorem excludes girth-five Petersen for k>=5. A complete k=5..7 mathematical implication comparison and synonym search found no dominating theorem; bibliographic uniqueness is not certified.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible exact prior homotopy calculation for Petersen k=5,6,7 might exist; searches do not prove priority.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical vertex-transitive Kneser graph and ordinary k-cut complexes form a natural finite filtration. A complete classification across every feasible cut size is motivated by the foundational 2023/2024 cut-complex research, not an arbitrary slice. The unique pure but nonshellable 5-cut stage with mixed homotopy S3 wedge five S4, sandwiched between single-dimension bouquets, is an informative structural boundary not determined by previously known k=2,3,4 results. No paper-sized generalization is claimed.
